Get started

Install the SDK

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Use the repository and its toolchainUse the packaged addonConfigure the editorContinue

There are two useful starting points: a checkout with the repository's pinned development tools, or the packaged addon inside your own Godot project. Use a checkout when learning from the examples or changing the SDK. Use the addon when you want the extension and build helpers alongside a game's own files.

Use the repository and its toolchain#

Install Nix with flakes enabled, clone the repository, and enter the development shell:

Shell
git clone https://github.com/wlitwin/odin_godot.git
cd odin_godot
nix develop

The shell supplies Odin, build tools, and the godot collection used by imports such as "godot:godot". It also sets GODOT to the engine executable. The repository currently targets Godot 4.7.x; use the version and toolchain recorded by the checkout you are building.

If the engine is installed elsewhere, enter the shell with its path:

Shell
GODOT=/absolute/path/to/godot nix develop

Build and run a small existing scene before creating a project:

Shell
bash build/build_scripts.sh tests/showcase
"$GODOT" --path tests/showcase

This checks that the compiler, extension, and engine agree. If it fails, resolve the build or loader error before adding your own scripts.

Use the packaged addon#

The distributable contains addons/odin_godot, including the core extension, bindings, build helpers, and templates. Get it from the repository's release distribution or build it from a checkout with nix build .#release.

Copy the addon into your game's res://addons/ directory. You still need an Odin compiler on PATH: the addon includes a prebuilt core, while your gameplay scripts are compiled for your project.

Follow adding Odin to an existing project for the scripts layout and build command. The distribution reference describes the package layout, native ABI compatibility, and platform validation.

Configure the editor#

When the editor is launched outside the development shell, set these project settings to absolute paths:

Setting Purpose
odin_godot/root SDK checkout or installed addon used as the godot collection
odin_godot/odin_bin Odin compiler used by editor builds
odin_godot/ols_bin Language server used for completion

The shell's ODIN_GODOT_ROOT serves the corresponding collection role for build helpers. Keep the editor and command-line build pointed at the same SDK.

Continue#

Write your first script, or read the full project wiring guide for manifests, boot registration, and the two-library native layout.
